Your guide will pick you up from the hotel and take you to Rio de Janeiro's historic center. The excursion explores the city's colonial past, royal history, religious traditions and the architecture of old Rio. The name Rio de Janeiro is linked to January 1502, when Guanabara Bay was mistaken for the mouth of a river; the city itself was founded in 1565.

The route takes in Candelária Church, built in 1775, São Bento Monastery with its Baroque architecture, and the Lapa Arches, constructed in 1732 as an aqueduct to carry water from the Carioca River to the city center. You will also see the Municipal Theatre, decorated by European artists.

Novembro Square is home to the Imperial Palace, Tiradentes Palace, an 1808 cathedral and a sixteenth-century Carmelite convent. You will then see Boticário Square, with old facades and mosaics framed by centuries-old trees, and the Metropolitan Cathedral, which can accommodate 20,000 people.

The excursion ends at Confeitaria Colombo, where you can order coffee, tea and pastries. After the program, your guide will take you back to the hotel.
